The Operator has failed to comply with the conditions set forth in the Order and is therefore in violation of OGA3259(1).

Comments: On Monday, 11/6/2023, I conducted a routine inspection of the PA Mineral Services, LLC O Gibson 5 well, permit number 005-26672. The well is located at the edge of a scrub brush field off of Campbell Run Road in Burrell township, Armstrong county. The well is in production and had a reported production of 1,425.0 mcf for 2022. There is a well id tag/well site id sign attached to the well head. A second well site id sign is posted on the production chart box. One brine tank was recently requested to be removed from the Hauger 1 well site (permit number 005-27698) and placed on this site (see pictures # 6 and 7). These actions have resulted in the operator being cited for a violation to OGA 3216(c) - Failure to fill all pits used to contain produced fluids or industrial wastes and remove unnecessary drilling supplies/equipment not needed for production within 9 months from completion of drilling of well.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 990698
Permit API: 051-20905
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Dunbar Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/29/2023
Comments: On March 29 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to an OGI request of the James Joshowtiz 12 OG Well.The findings were as follows:At the time of the inspection, The access road appeared to be stable with no signs of erosion or sedimentation issues. The well site exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. There were no erosion or sedimentation issues onsite. The well posting was present at the time of this inspection. There were no observed leaks or discharge on the ground or around the wellhead. The production tank appears to have a corrosive pipe connected to it that is actively leaking fluid. A soil conductivity reading was taken at the base of the production tank. The soil conductivity reading was 15.78mS were the active leaking fluid is occurring. A background soil conductivity reading was taken of 0.22 mS. The Department recommends that the Operator remediate the area as necessary in accordance with the Department's Spill Policy. The Department requests the operator provide a quantity of what was released, what specific fluids were released, and when and how the release occurred. The Department request that this information be provided in the NOV response. Based on today's observations, violations are being issued at this time.

SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.

Violation ID: 885918
Permit API: 063-36924
Unconventional: Yes
County: Indiana
Municipality: Cherryhill Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2020-05-28
Comments: On 5/27/2020 at 1101 hrs., Carey Bell with EQT Production Company called the Department to report a release of approximately 5 to 10 gallons of production fluids and hydraulic oil from a tank at EQT's Diamondville Pad in Cherryhill Twp., Indiana Co. I spoke with Ms. Bell and then with Logan Dominick, EQT's on-site Environmental Coordinator, on 5/27/2020. Mr. Dominick explained the nature of the release and also stated that EQT already had contractors onsite to remediate the release. I explained to Mr. Dominick that rather than conducting an on-site inspection and requesting that all personnel vacate the site (due to current Department Policy regarding COVID-19), I would rather have EQT submit documentation of the release and remediation and I would conduct an administrative inspection. Mr. Dominick supplied this documentation in an email on 5/28/2020 and both the email and attached summary will be uploaded to eFACTS. The following violations are being cited for the release of production fluid and hydraulic oil onto the ground: 78a.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(a), and SWMA 610(1). These violations are being cited against the most recently drilled well permit number (063-36924), as the ESCGP for this site has been terminated. The release area has been excavated and restored, and the tank has been placed back into service. The above violations will be resolved upon submission of a waste manifest to the Department for the excavated material and inspection of the site.

Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions after two produced fluid releases occurred over the past five months. The frac is still underway on the well pad. The well site secondary containment appears to be in good condition. No holes or crushed berms were observed. Craig Shores and Zach Burnett and Creston Consultant Reps., Will Dolan and Jason Rajan. Starting at approx. 10:00, ending annuli pressures were checked using a Digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. The bubbling dissipated when the (20x13) annulus was returned to venting via Sentry valve. - The 1HC, 2HC, 4H, 7H and the 101HC had water in the cellars, but below conductor casing. The 3H had water above the conductor casing. Slight bubbling was noted only in the 4H cellar. - All (6) wells (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened and venting to production tank and the (20x13) annuli were opened and venting to atmosphere via Sentry valves @ 12:05

Comments: On September 2, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in regards to violations issued under inspection report 4261627.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department did not observe an Act 9 sign. The Department recommends the operator install an Act 9 sign in accordance with 78a55. The Department also did not observe an Emergency Response Plan (ERP). The Department recommends the operator ensure an ERP is onsite in accordance with 78a55.Upon inspection of the well site, the 2 previously observed corroded production tanks were still present onsite. While the Department did not observe any active leaks at the time of this inspection, the Department observed orange staining and saturated dirt/gravel surrounding the corroded tank. Elevated soil conductivity readings were again obtained around the corroded production tank. Conductivity readings of 5.11ms, 6.24mS, 6.68mS, and OR (Over detectable range, >20mS). Prior to leaving the site, the Department spoke with operator representative Robert Inghram and inquired if there was a timeline for removal of the tanks and remediation of the impacted soil. Mr. Inghram stated that the NOV (IR 4261627) was received and an NOV response was being prepared to be submitted to the Department. With the preparation of the NOV response, the operator is finalizing a contractor to conduct the work and work would begin as soon as they can get it scheduled.Based on today's inspection, violations for the observed release, production equipment onsite not in use, no ERP onsite, and no Act 9 Sign onsite remain outstanding.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Blackhill Energy's Jackson A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 3/7/2023 at 0830 hours. The weather was 32 degrees with mostly clear skies. A layer of snow covered the majority of the site.Blackhill had additional excavation conducted since the previous inspection. Collected fluid in the excavated area from the release that occurred on 1/2/2023 was field measured for electrical conductivity and ranged from 2.25 to 2.5mS/cm today. The DEP recommends recovering the fluid in this area and disposing of it properly. Pooled water on the pad surface that was field measured for electrical conductivity outside of the known impacted area from the release on 1/2/2023 ranged from 560 to 960us/cm today. No additional evidence of spills/releases was observed outside of secondary containment today. Water flowing in the rock-lined channel along the northern edge of the expanded pad portion was field measured at ~860us/cm.The pad remains permanently stabilized with vegetation or temporarily stabilized with straw and erosion control blankets. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. Containment structures remain intact. No leaks or other structural issues were noted with any of the secondary containment liners today. The DEP recommends recovering any fluids in and outside of containment that are noted in the findings sections below. Violations cited against API #015-23733 on 1/3/2023 remain outstanding at this time. I departed the site at 1015 hours.

Comments: Well is equipped for production, and shut in at this time. City of Warren Fire Dept. notified the Office of Oil and Gas Management of an incident that occurred on the afternoon of 09/30/2024. It was stated that a lawnmower had damaged a gas line, causing a release of natural gas at the BJS,LLC Deluxe well pad. The fire department expressed concerns regarding emergency contact posting at the well site, which resulted in delayed response time in mitigating the gas release. During the course of inspection, it was noted that a site ID sign had been recently installed at the tank battery, which contained the operators name and emergency contact phone number. Operator address was absent from the sign. Permit number has not been affixed to the wellhead. The observed conditions constitute violations of Section 3211(g) and (h) of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act. Notice of Violations have been documented within this report.

Violation ID: 8228897
Permit API: 125-29133
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Blaine Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/09/2025
Comments: On April 9, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Schwotzer Arthur well site in Blaine Township, Washington County. An Erosion and Sediment (E and S) individual permit was issued by the Department for the site on January 26, 2024 and expires on January 25, 2029. This inspection was conducted in response to soil movement on the southwestern fill slope of the well pad and upslope of the northern corner of the well pad, which was reported to the Department by the operator on April 7, 2025. Range Resources representative Dennis Furmanek was present with the Department for this inspection. The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). Stimulation operations are ongoing at the well pad at the time of this inspection (see photos 3 and 18). All containers onsite that appear to store regulated substances are placed within well pad secondary containment (see photo 20). All secondary containment onsite appears to be in good condition at the time of inspection with no holes or tears observed. The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 23). The GPU units onsite are equipped with secondary containment (see photo 24). Some areas of minor staining were observed on the surface of the well pad during this inspection. The E and S inspection log, E and S plan drawings, Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention, and Contingency (PPC) plan, E and S individual permit approval letter, secondary containment inspection, log, and well permits are onsite (see photos 19 and 25). Upon review onsite, the ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the information required by 78a.55.The access road appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photo 2). The soil crack that was reported by the operator on 4/07/2025 was present on the southwestern fill slope of well pad (see photos 4-9). It appears to be approximately 15 feet in length with saturated ground down slope of it, and no toe bulge observed below at the time of inspection. The Schwotzer to Hoskins pipeline is being constructed west of the well pad (see photo 11). The slough that was also reported by the operator on 4/07/2025 was present up slope of the northern corner of well pad (see photos 12-16). The operator estimates this area of soil movement to be approximately 25 feet wide by 30 feet long. This slough appears to pose the potential to threaten a stormwater channel down slope of it, if the displaced soil continues to move (see photo 17). Mr. Furmanek reported during this inspection that the operator intends to conduct repairs on these areas of soil movement once stimulation operations have been completed onsite and weather conditions allow for it. CFS that appears to be in need of maintenance was observed along the northeastern edge of the well pad (see photo 21).Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends the operator conduct general maintenance and housekeeping onsite to address the minor staining onsite and CFS maintenance needed. The Department also recommends that the operator monitor the soil crack on the southwestern fill slope of the well pad for any additional soil movement and implement temporary stabilization on the soil exposed by the slough north of the well pad.Violations shall be issued against the slough north of the well pad which could pose the potential to threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth. See NOV Response Comments.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Blaine Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/09/2025
Comments: On April 9, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Schwotzer Arthur well site in Blaine Township, Washington County. An Erosion and Sediment (E and S) individual permit was issued by the Department for the site on January 26, 2024 and expires on January 25, 2029. This inspection was conducted in response to soil movement on the southwestern fill slope of the well pad and upslope of the northern corner of the well pad, which was reported to the Department by the operator on April 7, 2025. Range Resources representative Dennis Furmanek was present with the Department for this inspection. The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). Stimulation operations are ongoing at the well pad at the time of this inspection (see photos 3 and 18). All containers onsite that appear to store regulated substances are placed within well pad secondary containment (see photo 20). All secondary containment onsite appears to be in good condition at the time of inspection with no holes or tears observed. The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 23). The GPU units onsite are equipped with secondary containment (see photo 24). Some areas of minor staining were observed on the surface of the well pad during this inspection. The E and S inspection log, E and S plan drawings, Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention, and Contingency (PPC) plan, E and S individual permit approval letter, secondary containment inspection, log, and well permits are onsite (see photos 19 and 25). Upon review onsite, the ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the information required by 78a.55.The access road appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photo 2). The soil crack that was reported by the operator on 4/07/2025 was present on the southwestern fill slope of well pad (see photos 4-9). It appears to be approximately 15 feet in length with saturated ground down slope of it, and no toe bulge observed below at the time of inspection. The Schwotzer to Hoskins pipeline is being constructed west of the well pad (see photo 11). The slough that was also reported by the operator on 4/07/2025 was present up slope of the northern corner of well pad (see photos 12-16). The operator estimates this area of soil movement to be approximately 25 feet wide by 30 feet long. This slough appears to pose the potential to threaten a stormwater channel down slope of it, if the displaced soil continues to move (see photo 17). Mr. Furmanek reported during this inspection that the operator intends to conduct repairs on these areas of soil movement once stimulation operations have been completed onsite and weather conditions allow for it. CFS that appears to be in need of maintenance was observed along the northeastern edge of the well pad (see photo 21).Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends the operator conduct general maintenance and housekeeping onsite to address the minor staining onsite and CFS maintenance needed. The Department also recommends that the operator monitor the soil crack on the southwestern fill slope of the well pad for any additional soil movement and implement temporary stabilization on the soil exposed by the slough north of the well pad.Violations shall be issued against the slough north of the well pad which could pose the potential to threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth. See NOV Response Comments.

Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#373559).¿¿ ¿¿ ¿¿ The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, and possible failures.¿¿ As part of the investigation 1 slam bar hole approximately 1-2 feet from the well head was placed into the ground to identify if any methane was migrating from the well bore.¿¿3% LEL was detected in this slam bar hole. All valves are open and the well is currently equipped for production. Two check valves were in place in the production lines and were oriented correctly. Casing pressure was 0 P.S.I. and the tubing pressure was 0 P.S.I. ¿¿ Well records, production reports, and mechanical integrity assessment reports were reviewed to assist in the investigation. ¿¿ 100% Methane by volume was detected in the 8.625" X 6.625" annulus utilizing an MSA ALTAIR 5X Meter which was calibrated on 07/20/2023. A significant amount of bubbling could be herd in 8.625" X 6.625" annulus. Fumes were also visible flowing from the annulus. At approximately 11:00 the well was vented and the bubbling could no longer be heard. At approximately 11:36 the methane levels in the annulus dropped to 9% methane by volume. For safety reasons only one slam bar hole was placed in the ground on the windward side of the well bore due to the high amount of methane flowing from the annulus. 3% LEL was detected in this slam bar hole. The well was vented by a well tender during this inspection and a gas sample was collected from the vented casing string. As a result the following violations are being issued against this well. ¿¿ VIOLATION: 78.86 - CASING AND CEMENTING – DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. ¿¿ VIOLATION:78.73(a) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to construct and operate the well in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected. ¿¿ VIOLATION:78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS – MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well. ¿¿ VIOLATION: 78.81(a)1 - CASING AND CEMENTING – GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to allow for effective control of the well at all times. At this time, the Department is requesting an investigation into the possible source of methane to be conducted by the operator.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection at Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) well site located in Columbia, Springfield and Troy Townships, Bradford County on 7/16/2025 at 1020 hours. The weather was in the low 80 degrees F with partly cloudy skies. A representative with the DEP's Environmental Cleanups Program and a Repsol representative were present for the inspection. During the DEPs inspection, fluids field measured at >19.99mS/cm were noted within the secondary constructed berm (photo #2) and within the stormwater control basin (photo #3). Sheet flow of fluids off the edges of the pad surface have subsided. A pump was observed near the stormwater control basin that started recovering fluids held within the basin in the evening hours on 7/15/2025. The DEP continued the monitoring of fluids/soils at set monitoring points in various areas around the well site. Distressed vegetation was observed in areas on the fill slopes (photos #5 and 7) and downslope of the constructed "corner" berm (photo #4). Soils field measured at >4.00mS/cm were noted downslope of the western corner of the well pad, below the constructed "corner" berm, which were also noted on 7/14/2025 and 7/15/2025. A representative with Repsol walked us up to the 7H wellhead. Fluids were observed within the well cellar. As a result of the release, large amounts of sand were observed piled around the wellheads.Repsol is currently working on an estimated volume for the release and has began working on a remediation plan. Resource Environmental (Resource) continues to screen soils to determine surface impacts. At this time, with the exception of the soils off the western corner of the site (near the hedgerow) and along the surface waterline, Resource has not discovered any additional impacted surface soils downslope of the well pad. Repsol plans to construct some sort of stormwater controls downslope of impacted soils to prevent further impacts to the surface.Violations of the following remain outstanding against API #015-23892 at this time: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), 25 Pa. Code 78a.54, Clean Streams Law 401, and SWMA 301.The DEP departed the well site at 1200 hours. For information regarding the DEP's inspections on 7/14/2025 and 7/15/2025, please see inspection record #s 4012602 and 4013600, respectively.

The brine tank remains disconnected from the well equipment at the time of inspection (see photo 9). No evidence of leaks or distressed vegetation was observed where the disconnected line is located. The brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection, with no staining or distressed vegetation on the ground around it (see photos 7 and 8). The API number and a means to identify and/or contact the operator have not been posted onsite since the week of 3/03/2025. The potential sedimentation that was identified during the time of IR 3926868 was not observable during this inspection.The Department continues to recommend that the brine tank is removed from site if it is no longer in use for production, in accordance with OGA3216(C).Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued from IR 3872789 shall remain outstanding.

Comments: On December 15, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the WL Hopkins Well Site. The inspection was conducted in response to a request made by an PA DEP OGI during an inspection conducted on 12/15/2023 (Sub-SAIR# 3660126). At the time of inspection, the following was observed:Act 9 Sign Installed, however the Operator of Record does not appear to be correct. The associated PPC plan and ER plan on site have not been updated to reflect the change in ownership. (Photo 11 and 12)The COASTAL Drill Rig was on site and connected to the well. The drill rig and associated equipment was not placed within secondary containment. (Photo 1)I observed fluid on the well pad surrounding the WL Hopkins 590312 Well and drill rig. I also observed fluid within the well cellar. I collected conductivity readings of the fluid on the well pad and within the cellar, which result in elevated conductivity readings. I also observed what appeared to be a light colored crystallin substance deposited on the well pad rock adjacent to the standing fluid. The crystallin substance appears to be salt which suggest that the fluid has been on site long enough to begin evaporation. The amount of fluid on the well pad appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. At the time of inspection, the Department was not previously notified by the Operator of a release of fluid to the well pad. (Photo 2 thru 10)While I was on site, I contacted Operator representative Kevin Wright (CONSOL/Leatherwood) to relay my observations related to the fluid release and recommend that the Operator being remediation immediately. Mr. Wright indicated that the Operator added brine to the well to kill the well on 11/15/2023.I am requesting clarification of the activity, date and time of when the fluid was added to the well bore and all information/inspections related to the monitoring of the well between 11/15/2023 and 12/15/2023. I am also requesting clarification of the source of the fluid added to the well bore on or around 11/15/2023.Violation are being issued for the release (78a.54, 78a57(a), 91.34(a), SWMA 301, 78a66(b)1,78a(b)1(i), 78a66(b)1(ii), 78a66(b)(2), 91.33(a) and 91.33(b).Violations are being issued for the failure to develop a site specific PPC plan and ER Plan. 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(c). 78a55(h).Violations are being issued for the failure to properly update the Act 9 Sign (78a55(i)(4)(D)(III).Violations are being issued for the failure to install secondary containment. (78a64(a))

Comments: On 3/27/2026, the Department conducted an inspection at the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection follows up to IR 4000998, where violations were left outstanding due to no observable Act 9 sign and available Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. Also, at the time of this inspection, no response of any kind has been received from the operator regarding violations issued in 3093059 or any subsequent cleanup that may have been conducted. At the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil. At the time of IR 3978494, no staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the production tanks.The following was observed:No Act 9 sign is present at the well site entrance, and no ERP was found anywhere onsite (photo 1). The production tanks appear to be sound at the time of inspection, with no evidence of fluids leaking to the ground around them. However, they still lack compliant secondary containment to 78a.64(a), as is required at unconventional well sites (photos 4 and 6). No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the gas well (photo 8). The well postings onsite include contact information for Dorso LP (photos 5 and 7). Outstanding violations issued against the operator's posted information are being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.The additional piping and production equipment that does not appear to be in use remains onsite (photos 10 and 11). Therefore, a violation shall be issued in IR 4170358 for failure to remove equipment that is not necessary for production, in accordance with in accordance with OGA3216(C).The well site overall exhibits greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion and sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (photo 2).Based on observations from this inspection, violations that were continued in IR 4000998 shall remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since the date of that inspection and no response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

Violation ID: 944664
Permit API: 015-23116
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Columbia Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/09/2022
Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of Repsol's VanBlarcom R 03-113 well site located in Columbia Township, Bradford County on 2/9/2022 at 1025 hours. The weather was 34 degrees with partly cloudy skies. This inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by the operator. Complaint ID #362029 is tied to the release within CTS. On 2/6/2022 at approximately 1500 hours a release of approximately 15 gallons of produced water and 3 gallons of glycol were released to the pad surface. A leaking produced water flow-line released the produced water directly beneath where the leak occurred. Insulation on the flow-line contained the released to the small area beneath the line. The release on the produced water flow-line caused a crack on a pex pipe near the GPU unit which released the glycol to the pad surface. Both areas were observed today having snow, ice and slush removed from the pad surface. It appears as though the snow absorbed the majority of the releases. I collected some snow beneath the produced water flow-line and allowed it to melt. The melted snow was field measured at ~155us/cm. The releases are both cleaned up to visible (photos #5 & 6). Barrels containing the impacted material were observed in the GPU secondary containment (photo #4). I spoke with Mark Watson (Repsol) over the phone while I was onsite. He explained that a leaking pipe on the produced water flow-line caused fluid to kick back, cracking a pex pipe on the GPU. The leaking produced water flow-line was reported to release ~15 gallons of produced water to the pad surface. The cracked pex pipe was reported to release ~3 gallons of glycol to the pad surface. Both areas were reported to be cleaned up to visible. Golder (environmental consultant) screened the areas on 2/7/2022, confirming that the releases had been remediated. I also spoke with Megan Depew (Repsol) over the phone who explained that the areas were hard to access for heavier equipment to excavate so the remediation work was conducted by hand. All impacted snow/ice/slush was placed into barrels and placed on secondary containment awaiting disposal. Based on the findings of today's inspection and Repsol's timely reporting and remediation of the releases, violations of the following are cited as immediately corrected against API # 015-23116: 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a) 35 P.S. 6018.301 I departed the site at 1200 hours.

Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of Repsol's VanBlarcom R 03-113 well site located in Columbia Township, Bradford County on 2/9/2022 at 1025 hours. The weather was 34 degrees with partly cloudy skies. This inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by the operator. Complaint ID #362029 is tied to the release within CTS. On 2/6/2022 at approximately 1500 hours a release of approximately 15 gallons of produced water and 3 gallons of glycol were released to the pad surface. A leaking produced water flow-line released the produced water directly beneath where the leak occurred. Insulation on the flow-line contained the released to the small area beneath the line. The release on the produced water flow-line caused a crack on a pex pipe near the GPU unit which released the glycol to the pad surface. Both areas were observed today having snow, ice and slush removed from the pad surface. It appears as though the snow absorbed the majority of the releases. I collected some snow beneath the produced water flow-line and allowed it to melt. The melted snow was field measured at ~155us/cm. The releases are both cleaned up to visible (photos #5 & 6). Barrels containing the impacted material were observed in the GPU secondary containment (photo #4). I spoke with Mark Watson (Repsol) over the phone while I was onsite. He explained that a leaking pipe on the produced water flow-line caused fluid to kick back, cracking a pex pipe on the GPU. Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the JKLM Sweden Valley 107 well pad located in Sweden Twp, Potter Co. on 6/3/2019 @1115 hours in response to notification of a spill, reported to the Department on 5/31/2019 @1535 hours. The weather was sunny, 54 degrees, winds WSW 5mph, gusts 10mph. Present onsite for the inspection were Terra Tokarz, Whipper Hill Consulting and Matt Skolny, JKLM. CTS report# 342615 states, JKLM reported a hose broke while pumping production water from the production water tank to the tank farm releasing approximately 3 to 4 barrels of production water; released water overwhelmed pump containment and spilled to gravel (soil/concrete) surface; JKLM utilized on-site vac truck to recover fluid. The following onsite conditions were observed during the inspection. The pump had been moved approximately 15' from the original spill location in order to allow for excavation of pad material impacted during the spill. Onsite personnel stated a valve, on a pump component, was left open while the operator traveled to another site to check on a different water transfer. This allowed the suction line from the pump to discharge production fluid, from the production tanks on the SV107, into it's secondary containment. The fluid over-topped the containment discharging an estimated 3 barrels of production fluid onto the pad surface. The fluid was recovered with a vacuum truck. Approximately 2-4" of pad material in a 35' x 70' area was excavated after a grid screening for conductivity, and placed in waste containers onsite. Penn E&R arrived onsite to collect confirmatory samples during the inspection. Violations of the following regulations are cited at this time: 25 Pa Code 78a.57 CSL 402(b) SWMA 301 I departed the site at 1245 hours.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a INCIDENT inspection at the Tilden Marcellus -Pierson 801 Well Pad located in Gaines Twp, Tioga Co. on 9/30/2019 @1300 hours in response to spill notification# 345263. The weather was 72 degrees, light rain. The spill notification report states, "Regina Logue, Regulatory/Environmental Manager for Tilden Marcellus LLC notified the phone duty officer that a spill of production water from a defective tee in a dump line occurred on 9/28/2019 at 0830 hours. The spill of 1.5 barrels occurred on the well pad. Tilden employees used a vac truck to remove liquid. Lined dumpsters and an excavator are on the way for cleanup. Tilden's well tender will be overseeing the cleanup." As of today's inspection, the area of the spill appears to be backfilled with gravel. Standing fluid on the pad surface in the area of the release had a field measured conductivity of "Over Range" or >19.99mS/cm. A visible flow path, from the spill location, down the fill slope through the vegetation was observed. A "Growline" soil conductivity meter was then used to test the soils in the vicinity of the flow path. The soil readings were >4.0mS/cm which is the max range of the soil meter. The elevated soil conductivity readings reached the area, at the base of the fill slope, beneath a large conifer tree. I immediately left the site to contact my Supervisor, Matt Nuss, to notify him of my findings. Report Details
Inspection Client: GREYLOCK PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78a66(b)2 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases - Operator or other responsible party failed to contact the appropriate regional Department office by telephone or call the Department’s Statewide toll free number as soon as practicable, but no later than 2 hours after discovering the spill or release.
Violation ID: 8264366
Permit API: 059-25724
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Cumberland Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/10/2026
Comments: On 02/10/2026, an incident inspection was conducted following notification of a spill that occurred on 2/09/2026 from Greylock (CTS #395045). I was accompanied by Madison Raviart (PA DEP Water Quality Specialist) and Greylock representative Trevor Wood. Per Greylock, the spill was reported to the Department's emergency hotline on 02/09/2026. It was reported that 1-3 bbls of brine water released onto the pad on 02/09/2026. The spill was identified at 4:00 PM and reported to the hotline at approximately 7:13 PM. Gravel and snow was impacted on the pad and the spill was contained to the pad and snow was hand shoveled into tanks containment. No waters of the Commonwealth were impacted. The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. There was no Emergency Response Plan or The Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency plan onsite at the site entrance (Photo 1). I recommend these be added to site near the site entrance. The access road appeared to be in generally good condition and maintained (Photo 2).Cinders were placed on road coming up to the pad on 02/10/2026 (Photos 3-5). Snow around the containment for the tanks was hand shoveled and put into the containment (Photo 6). The spill originated from a separator on the pad. High pressure caused brine water to come out of the separator and spray onto the pad and tank. 1-3 barrels (bbls) were released (Photos 7-10). Conductivity readings taken in the middle of the impacted area ranged from 2.09 mS/cm-4.55mS/cm (Photos 11,12). Conductivity reading taken in gravel on the opposite side of the entrance in front of separators was 252 S/cm (Photo 13). Conductivity readings taken along tank containment ranged from 709 S/cm-8.61 mS/cm (Photos 14-18).The area was still in the process of remediation and Greylock was waiting on additional equipment to begin remediation. The spill appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. I recommend following Act 2 guidelines.Due to the release of brine water and no Emergency Response Plan or The Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency plan onsite, violations of 78a.54, 78a57(a), SWMA 301, 91.34(a), 78A55(I)5I, and 78a66(b)2.
